name: gantt
import: import { Gantt, type GanttTask, type GanttDependency } from '@absoluteui/components/gantt';
purpose: A project schedule: a task tree grid (name, start, end, duration, progress, resources, float) beside a timeline of bars with summary tasks, milestones, progress, baselines, dependency connectors, the critical path, non-working days, and today. Tasks are scheduled in working days of a Business Calendar: dependencies (finish-to-start, start-to-start, finish-to-finish, start-to-finish, with lag or lead) push successors later, never before their requested start; manual tasks keep their start and report violated dependencies. Editing: drag a bar to move it, its end to resize it, its link handle onto another bar to link them; Ctrl/Cmd+Left/Right moves by a working day, Shift+Left/Right changes the duration, and the toolbar offers the same plus Link (then Enter on the successor). Every change is dispatched first as the cancelable aui-task-change with the tasks, dependencies, and new schedule; changes are undoable. An optional resource histogram shows daily load against capacity. Rows are virtual. The engine (scheduleGantt, resourceLoad, createsCycle) is pure and runs without DOM (for example on a server).
whenToUse: Planning and tracking projects with dependent tasks, milestones, and deadlines.
Finding the critical path and the float of each task after a change.
Comparing the current schedule with a baseline, and spotting over-allocated resources.
whenNotToUse: Calendars of meetings and appointments with times of day: use Scheduler.
Workflow boards without dates: use Kanban.
Simple date ranges on a few rows: use a timeline view of Scheduler or a table.
responsive: The body scrolls in two dimensions inside a fixed block size (--aui-gantt-height, 32rem) while the page reflows at 320 px (WCAG 1.4.10 exception for two-dimensional content). The tree grid (--aui-gantt-table-width, 28rem) stays at the inline start while the timeline scrolls; in containers narrower than 40rem it scrolls away with the timeline. The header rows are sticky. Toolbar buttons are touch-target-min squares; bars, resize edges, and link handles use touch-action: none.
rtl: direction 'rtl' mirrors the timeline (dates run from right to left, connectors are mirrored) and swaps ArrowLeft/ArrowRight: expand/collapse and Ctrl/Cmd or Shift + arrow follow the reading direction (the arrow toward later dates moves later or lengthens).
theme: Bars use a tint of color-chart-1..8 (from the task color) over color-surface with a solid accent border and a solid progress fill; critical bars get a color-error-fg border-width-strong border and a hatch pattern (not color alone, and the grid says 'Critical'); manual tasks have dashed borders; summary bars are color-text brackets; milestones are diamonds; baselines are thin color-text-muted bars. Connectors use color-chart-axis (critical: color-error-fg; violated: dashed color-warning-fg). Non-working days are color-surface-sunken; today is a dashed color-primary line. Over-capacity days in the histogram use color-error-fg with a hatch. Forced colors use Canvas/CanvasText bars, Mark for critical, and Highlight for focus and the link source.
timezone: Dates are PlainDate values (no timezone); durations and lags count working days of the calendar. The default today is the local date of the device (pass today to fix it).
security: Task, resource, and dependency text renders through textContent. Options are validated (unique ids, known parents and resources, no cycles, dependencies between leaf tasks only) before use (GANTT_OPTIONS). Positions and sizes are written through the CSSOM only (CSP-safe); connectors are SVG paths built from numbers.
dataHandling: No persistence, network access, or telemetry. Changes are reported through aui-task-change (tasks, dependencies, schedule) for the application to save; the task's start is the requested start and the scheduled dates are in schedule.

budgets.budget: < 150 ms in headless Chromium (e2e performance test)

budgets.metric: Keyboard move of a task with 2,000 tasks (reschedule and render)
budgets.budget: < 60 ms in headless Chromium (e2e performance test)
< 80 ms in headless Chromium (e2e performance test)

performance.testedScale: 2,000 visible tasks (10,000 in the engine budget) for the budgets; 6 to 2,000 tasks in the unit tests. Rows are virtual; timeline columns are not (a day scale over several years renders a long scale).

limitations: Scheduling is in whole working days (PlainDate); hours within a day are not modeled.
Dependencies connect leaf tasks only; summary tasks follow their children.
Auto-scheduled tasks start at their requested start or later (as soon as dependencies allow); there are no other constraint types (must finish on, as late as possible).
Resource load is reported, not leveled: over-allocations are shown but not resolved.
Progress is displayed but not edited in the chart.
Pointer drags are not announced step by step (keyboard and toolbar changes are).
Manual screen-reader verification (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver) is pending.
unsupported: Adding, deleting, renaming, indenting, or reordering tasks inside the chart (change tasks with update()).
Several calendars (per resource or per task).
Split tasks, recurring tasks, and cost tracking.
antiPatterns: Writing the scheduled dates back into task.start after every change: the requested start becomes a floor and tasks can no longer move earlier when predecessors do.
Passing new tasks on every framework render: it clears the undo history.
Relying on the timeline for information: keep the grid columns users need (start, end, duration) visible.

adapters.angular: @absoluteui/angular/gantt: generated AuiGantt directive ([auiGantt], inputs mirror GanttOptions; outputs auiTaskChange, auiTaskActivate, auiExpandChange, auiScaleChange; controllerSignal).
adapters.react: @absoluteui/react/gantt: generated AuiGantt (props = GanttOptions + onTaskChange, onTaskActivate, onExpandChange, onScaleChange; ref receives the Gantt).
adapters.vue: @absoluteui/vue/gantt: generated AuiGantt (emits taskChange, taskActivate, expandChange, scaleChange; template ref exposes controller).
